sources.entry: If you have any suggestions, ideas, or discover excellent software, feel free to submit a PR to help improve this list. Please read the contributing guidelines before contributing. We also welcome you to continue following this awesome list to build a better macOS tool collection together.

summary.one_liner: The "awesome" meta-list: a large curated index of links to resources, tools, and learning material across programming languages, platforms, computer science, and other topics, maintained by sindresorhus.
summary.what_it_does: This repository is an awesome list, so it is itself a collection of links rather than a software project. Its README is a long, flat-to-nested bulleted list of categories such as Platforms, Programming Languages, Front-End and Back-End Development, Computer Science, Databases, Security, Gaming, Hardware, and Miscellaneous, each with a short description and links to other awesome lists or resources. It also has a Related section pointing to other awesome-list tools and indexes. The README text shown is mostly category names and one-line descriptions, with many entries lacking visible URLs in the extracted text. The list is organized by topic, not by any single tool or codebase.
use_cases: Finding curated resources for a programming language or framework
Browsing learning materials across computer science topics
Discovering other awesome lists by topic
Looking up tools for web front-end or back-end development
Exploring security, hardware, or data science resources
Starting point for researching a new technology area
notable: Topic-organized index spanning software, hardware, science, and business
Includes a Related section linking to other awesome-list discovery tools
Each category has short one-line descriptions of what it covers
Contribution guide and list-creation guidance referenced in the README
caveats: Extracted README shows category names and descriptions; many entries have no visible links in the text, so the page must be read on GitHub for URLs
Not a software tool; nothing to install or run
Some entries are brief or dated, so individual links may go stale
